answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from pricing each identity above the value it can extract: agents post stake, complete verifiable work, and build reputation over time, so spinning up a marble of throwaway accounts buys no cheap influence. Honest agents are re-audited by peers on every payout, and a vertex of fabricated history fails the moment rewards demand checkable output instead of mere activity. Every clone costs compute, locked stake, and waiting time, while real agents compound trust; the velvet an attacker assembles therefore costs more than the rewards it could ever harvest
